chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَرَ، الْغِفَارِيُّ، أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ، (مَدَنِيٌّ). يُلْقَى عَلَيْهِ الْفَاسِدُ كَثِيرًا. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ). وَيُجَازُ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ شَاهِدًا.

translations.en: Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi Umar, al-Ghifari, Abu Muhammad, (Medinan). Much corruption is cast upon him. He narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). It is permissible for him to be brought out as a witness.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Du‘afā* highlights the nuanced evaluation of ʿAbdullāh ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ghifārī, a Medinan narrator of Imam al-Ṣādiq (AS). Although deemed permissible to testify with (*yujāzu an yukhraja shāhidan*), he is noted for frequent errors or corruption (*al-fāsid*), illustrating the critical methodology of *al-jarḥ wa al-taʿdīl* in assessing hadith reliability.
en.seo_question: Who is Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Ghifari in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.الْفَاسِدُ: The corrupted one (a technical term for a narrator whose narrations are mixed with errors or fabrications)
key_terms.شَاهِدًا: Witness (one whose testimony is accepted in legal contexts)
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
